title: Men Don't Protect You Anymore Wooden Postcard

description.main: A wooden postcard from Printed Matter carrying one sentence from Jenny Holzer's Survival series (1983-85), printed in red capitals across the grain of a thin sheet of wood. The text reads MEN DON'T PROTECT YOU ANYMORE; the line was written for electronic signs and later appeared on plaques, T-shirts and benches.
description.extended:
A wooden postcard from Printed Matter carrying one sentence from Jenny Holzer's Survival series (1983-85), printed in red capitals across the grain of a thin sheet of wood.

The text reads MEN DON'T PROTECT YOU ANYMORE. Holzer wrote the Survival texts for electronic signs, after her first Spectacolor board in Times Square in 1982, and the sentences soon moved onto aluminium plaques, T-shirts and caps, and later onto stone benches. A 1984 plaque of this line stood on the sculpture plinth of Berlin's Museumsinsel from 2020. Printed Matter publishes the postcard with the artist at 10 x 15 cm, digitally printed, in a line of wooden postcards drawn from the Truisms and Survival series.

Holzer (b. 1950) began with the Truisms of 1977-79, anonymous broadsheets wheat-pasted around Manhattan, then the Inflammatory Essays (1979-82) and the Living plaques (1981). She won the Golden Lion at the 1990 Venice Biennale and has projected text onto buildings since 2001. The library also holds her Ivorypress box Belligerent (2017).
description.artist_bio: Jenny Holzer (b. 1950, Gallipolis, Ohio) has worked with written language in public space since the Truisms street posters of 1977-79. Her work has appeared on LED signs, plaques, benches, T-shirts and as light projections on buildings and landscape. She won the Golden Lion at the 1990 Venice Biennale and has had major shows at the Guggenheim museums in New York and Bilbao and the Whitney Museum of American Art.

notes: Acquired from Printed Matter, New York: https://www.printedmatter.org/catalog/14304. Not signed. Red-text variant ([Red Text] on the Printed Matter record); a black-text printing of this phrase also exists, though in October 2026 printedmatter.org listed only the red. Printed Matter stock 112927, process Digital, published with the artist (Printed Matter Inc. / J. Holzer). Text from the Survival series, 1983-85. The Printed Matter record gives no publication year, so year is left empty; an auction record (Chiswick Auctions, via Invaluable) dates a pair of these Survival wooden postcards to 1994.
